title: Think positive!
paragraphs: How are you feeling today? If your head’s in a spin because you’ve had a bad night's sleep, or you’re hungover, or maybe you’ve just got too much to do, the chances are you’re not in the best of moods. If everything seems like an effort and you have a negative attitude, the last thing you want to be told it to ‘be positive!’ But having this mindset could have more benefits than you think.

Of course, developing a positive attitude is easier said than done – it doesn’t come naturally to everyone. When you’re feeling down in the dumps, it is hard to be optimistic. But a study in the US has found that people who are optimists are more likely to live longer than those who have a more negative approach to life. It revealed the likelihood of positive people living to the age of 85 or more to be higher. So, maybe the thought of a longer life might encourage you to have a more hopeful outlook on life.

The study concluded that optimists may find it easier to control emotions and get less stressed. And as stress impacts on the immune system, it’s possible that optimists cope better with infections. Professor Lewina Lee from Boston University School of Medicine, who worked on the study, told the BBC that: "Our findings speak to the possibility that raising levels of optimism may promote longevity and healthy ageing." And she advises that pessimists could benefit from doing things like imagining a future where everything turns out well.

But if you’re a ‘glass half empty’ type of person, could seeing the world through rose-tinted glasses work for you? Accepting that we all have problems and that we’re not all the same helps us to get a grip on our emotions. Some people say it’s best to celebrate the positives and not dwell on the negative parts of our lives.

People have being giving the BBC their personal advice on keeping a healthy and positive approach to life: Vicki Siska says "Music feeds my soul, a sense of humour keeps things in perspective, and I have good friends who love and care for me." And Pippa Kennedy says "being grateful for what you have - and lots of chocolate - helps!" The saying goes that ‘a healthy body leads a healthy mind’ which is probably why other people have recommended doing yoga and meditation as well as staying fit and healthy to help maintain a positive outlook on life.

vocabulary.entry: head’s in a spin /hedz ɪn ə spɪn/ 晕头转向；头脑发昏
vocabulary.example: I've got so many emails to answer, my head's in a spin.
vocabulary.translation: 我有一大堆邮件要回复，搞得晕头转向。

vocabulary.entry: hungover /ˈhʌŋəʊvə(r)/ adj. 宿醉未醒的
vocabulary.example: He stayed in bed all morning, feeling hungover.
vocabulary.translation: 他整个上午都躺在床上，宿醉未醒。

vocabulary.entry: in the best of moods /ɪn ðə best ɒv muːdz/ 心情极佳
vocabulary.example: She's in the best of moods today because she got a promotion.
vocabulary.translation: 她今天心情好极了，因为她升职了。

vocabulary.entry: positive attitude /ˈpɒzətɪv ˈætɪtjuːd/ 积极态度
vocabulary.example: Having a positive attitude can help you overcome many difficulties.
vocabulary.translation: 保持积极的态度可以帮你克服很多困难。

vocabulary.entry: mindset /ˈmaɪndset/ n. 心态；思维模式
vocabulary.example: It's hard to change someone's fixed mindset.
vocabulary.translation: 改变一个人固有的思维模式很难。

vocabulary.entry: easier said than done /ˈiːziə sed ðæn dʌn/ 说起来容易做起来难
vocabulary.example: Saving money is easier said than done for most young people.
vocabulary.translation: 对大多数年轻人来说，存钱是说起来容易做起来难。

vocabulary.entry: down in the dumps /daʊn ɪn ðə dʌmps/ 情绪低落；郁郁寡欢
vocabulary.example: He's been down in the dumps since he failed the exam.
vocabulary.translation: 自从考试不及格后，他就一直郁郁寡欢。

vocabulary.entry: optimist /ˈɒptɪmɪst/ n. 乐观主义者
vocabulary.example: My father is an optimist who always looks on the bright side of things.
vocabulary.translation: 我爸爸是个乐观主义者，总是看事情好的一面。

vocabulary.entry: likelihood /ˈlaɪklihʊd/ n. 可能性
vocabulary.example: There is a high likelihood of rain tomorrow.
vocabulary.translation: 明天很有可能下雨。

vocabulary.entry: hopeful outlook /ˈhəʊpfəl ˈaʊtlʊk/ 充满希望的态度
vocabulary.example: She has a hopeful outlook on the future of the company.
vocabulary.translation: 她对公司的未来抱有充满希望的态度。

vocabulary.entry: impact on /ˈɪmpækt ɒn/ 对……产生影响
vocabulary.example: Air pollution has a negative impact on people's health.
vocabulary.translation: 空气污染会对人们的健康产生负面影响。

vocabulary.entry: immune system /ɪˈmjuːn ˈsɪstəm/ 免疫系统
vocabulary.example: A balanced diet helps strengthen the immune system.
vocabulary.translation: 均衡的饮食有助于增强免疫系统。

vocabulary.entry: cope with /kəʊp wɪð/ 应对；处理
vocabulary.example: It's important to learn how to cope with stress in daily life.
vocabulary.translation: 学会在日常生活中应对压力很重要。

vocabulary.entry: infection /ɪnˈfekʃn/ n. 感染；传染病
vocabulary.example: The wound became red and swollen, showing signs of infection.
vocabulary.translation: 伤口红肿起来，显示出感染的迹象。

vocabulary.entry: promote longevity /prəˈməʊt lɒnˈdʒevəti/ 促进长寿
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise and a healthy diet can promote longevity.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动和健康饮食可以促进长寿。

vocabulary.entry: healthy ageing /ˈhelθi ˈeɪdʒɪŋ/ 健康老龄化
vocabulary.example: The government has launched a program to support healthy ageing.
vocabulary.translation: 政府推出了一项支持健康老龄化的计划。

vocabulary.entry: pessimist /ˈpesɪmɪst/ n. 悲观主义者
vocabulary.example: She's a pessimist who always expects the worst to happen.
vocabulary.translation: 她是个悲观主义者，总是往最坏的方面想。

vocabulary.entry: glass half empty /ɡlɑːs hɑːf ˈempti/ 杯子半空（指悲观的视角）
vocabulary.example: He always sees the glass as half empty, no matter how good things are.
vocabulary.translation: 不管事情多好，他总是用悲观的眼光看待。

vocabulary.entry: see through rose-tinted glasses /siː θruː rəʊz ˈtɪntɪd ˈɡlɑːsɪz/ 用过于乐观的眼光看待
vocabulary.example: Don't see the world through rose-tinted glasses; it has both good and bad sides.
vocabulary.translation: 不要用过于乐观的眼光看待世界，它既有好的一面也有坏的一面。

vocabulary.entry: get a grip on /ɡet ə ɡrɪp ɒn/ 掌控；控制
vocabulary.example: You need to get a grip on your temper and stop getting angry so easily.
vocabulary.translation: 你得控制一下自己的脾气，别动不动就发火。

vocabulary.entry: dwell on /dwel ɒn/ 纠结于；老是想着
vocabulary.example: It's no use dwelling on past mistakes; you should focus on the future.
vocabulary.translation: 纠结于过去的错误没有用，你应该着眼于未来。

vocabulary.entry: keep things in perspective /kiːp θɪŋz ɪn pəˈspektɪv/ 正确看待事物
vocabulary.example: Having a hobby helps you keep things in perspective when work is stressful.
vocabulary.translation: 当工作压力大的时候，培养一个爱好能帮你正确看待事物。

sentences.english: If your head’s in a spin because you’ve had a bad night's sleep, or you’re hungover, or maybe you’ve just got too much to do, the chances are you’re not in the best of moods.
sentences.chinese: 如果因为昨晚没睡好、宿醉未醒，或是手头事情太多而头晕目眩，那么你的心情大概率不会太好。

sentences.english: If everything seems like an effort and you have a negative attitude, the last thing you want to be told it to ‘be positive!’

sentences.english: But having this mindset could have more benefits than you think.
sentences.chinese: 但保持积极的心态，带来的好处可能比你想象的要多得多。

sentences.english: Of course, developing a positive attitude is easier said than done – it doesn’t come naturally to everyone.
sentences.chinese: 当然，培养积极心态说起来容易做起来难——并非每个人都能天生拥有这种心态。

sentences.english: When you’re feeling down in the dumps, it is hard to be optimistic.
sentences.chinese: 当你情绪低落时，想要乐观起来并不容易。

sentences.english: But a study in the US has found that people who are optimists are more likely to live longer than those who have a more negative approach to life.
sentences.chinese: 但美国的一项研究发现，乐观主义者比生活态度更消极的人更有可能长寿。

sentences.english: It revealed the likelihood of positive people living to the age of 85 or more to be higher.
sentences.chinese: 研究显示，心态积极的人活到85岁及以上的概率更高。

sentences.english: So, maybe the thought of a longer life might encourage you to have a more hopeful outlook on life.
sentences.chinese: 所以，或许一想到能更长寿，你就会更愿意用充满希望的眼光看待生活。

sentences.english: The study concluded that optimists may find it easier to control emotions and get less stressed.
sentences.chinese: 这项研究得出结论：乐观的人或许更容易控制情绪，感受到的压力也更小。

sentences.english: And as stress impacts on the immune system, it’s possible that optimists cope better with infections.
sentences.chinese: 而由于压力会影响免疫系统，乐观主义者可能更善于应对感染。

sentences.english: Professor Lewina Lee from Boston University School of Medicine, who worked on the study, told the BBC that: "Our findings speak to the possibility that raising levels of optimism may promote longevity and healthy ageing."
sentences.chinese: 参与该研究的波士顿大学医学院教授勒维娜·李向英国广播公司表示：“我们的研究结果表明，提升乐观程度有可能促进长寿和健康老龄化。”

sentences.english: And she advises that pessimists could benefit from doing things like imagining a future where everything turns out well.
sentences.chinese: 她还建议，悲观主义者可以尝试一些方法，比如想象一个一切都向好发展的未来，这会对他们有所帮助。

sentences.english: But if you’re a ‘glass half empty’ type of person, could seeing the world through rose-tinted glasses work for you?
sentences.chinese: 但如果你是那种“杯子里的水只剩一半”的悲观主义者，用过于乐观的眼光看待世界对你来说会有用吗？

sentences.english: Accepting that we all have problems and that we’re not all the same helps us to get a grip on our emotions.
sentences.chinese: 接受每个人都会遇到难题、每个人都各有不同的事实，有助于我们掌控自己的情绪。

sentences.english: Some people say it’s best to celebrate the positives and not dwell on the negative parts of our lives.
sentences.chinese: 有人说，最好的做法是多肯定生活中的积极面，不要一味纠结于消极的部分。

sentences.english: People have being giving the BBC their personal advice on keeping a healthy and positive approach to life: Vicki Siska says "Music feeds my soul, a sense of humour keeps things in perspective, and I have good friends who love and care for me."
sentences.chinese: 人们纷纷向英国广播公司分享了自己保持健康积极生活态度的个人心得：维基·西斯卡说：“音乐滋养我的灵魂，幽默感帮我正确看待事物，我还有一群爱我、关心我的好朋友。”
underlinedTerms: keeping a healthy and positive approach to life

sentences.english: And Pippa Kennedy says "being grateful for what you have - and lots of chocolate - helps!"
sentences.chinese: 皮帕·肯尼迪则表示：“对自己所拥有的一切心怀感恩——再加上多吃点巧克力——会很有帮助！”

sentences.english: The saying goes that ‘a healthy body leads a healthy mind’ which is probably why other people have recommended doing yoga and meditation as well as staying fit and healthy to help maintain a positive outlook on life.
sentences.chinese: 有句谚语说“健全的精神寓于健康的身体”，这或许就是为什么还有人建议，通过练习瑜伽、冥想以及保持身体健康，来帮助维持积极的生活态度。
